name: Senso-ji Temple
description: Tokyo's oldest and most famous Buddhist temple in Asakusa, approached through the iconic Kaminarimon thunder gate.

name: Tokyo Skytree
description: The tallest structure in Japan, offering sweeping observation-deck views of the city and, on clear days, Mount Fuji.

name: Meiji Shrine
description: A serene Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji, set within a forested park near Harajuku, popular for traditional weddings.

name: Shibuya Crossing
description: The world's busiest pedestrian scramble crossing, surrounded by neon billboards and the statue of the loyal dog Hachiko.

name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
description: A spacious park blending French, English, and Japanese garden styles, especially beloved for cherry blossoms in spring.

name: Tokyo Tower
description: A red-and-white Eiffel-inspired broadcasting tower in Minato, a nostalgic Tokyo landmark with two observation decks.

name: Tsukiji Outer Market
description: A lively food market street near the old fish market site, packed with stalls selling fresh sushi, grilled seafood, and street snacks.

name: Akihabara Electric Town
description: Tokyo's hub for electronics, anime, manga, and gaming culture, lined with multi-story stores and maid cafés.

name: Ueno Park & Museums
description: A large public park housing the Tokyo National Museum, a zoo, and hundreds of cherry trees, a cultural hub in one place.

name: Ginza
description: Tokyo's upscale shopping district, known for flagship department stores, luxury boutiques, and traditional craft shops.

name: Imperial Palace East Gardens
description: The public gardens on the former site of Edo Castle, next to the still-occupied Imperial Palace grounds, free to enter.

name: Harajuku & Takeshita Street
description: The center of Tokyo's youth fashion and pop culture, a narrow pedestrian street packed with quirky shops and crepe stands.

name: Odaiba
description: A futuristic man-made island in Tokyo Bay with shopping malls, a Ferris wheel, a life-size Gundam statue, and Rainbow Bridge views.

name: Roppongi Hills & Mori Art Museum
description: A high-rise complex combining shopping, dining, and a contemporary art museum with panoramic city views from the observation deck.

name: Yanaka Ginza
description: An old-town shopping street that survived WWII bombing, retaining a nostalgic, low-rise Tokyo atmosphere with cats and local snacks.

name: Nakamise Shopping Street
description: A traditional shopping street leading to Senso-ji Temple, lined with stalls selling snacks, crafts, and souvenirs since the Edo period.

name: Inokashira Park, Kichijoji
description: A large park with a central pond for boat rentals, near the trendy Kichijoji neighborhood and the Ghibli Museum.

name: Tokyo National Museum
description: Japan's oldest and largest museum, holding the world's most comprehensive collection of Japanese art and antiquities.

name: Ghibli Museum, Mitaka
description: A whimsical museum designed by Studio Ghibli, showcasing the artistry behind Japan's beloved animated films; tickets must be booked in advance.

name: Mount Takao
description: A forested mountain on Tokyo's western edge with hiking trails, a cable car, and a hilltop temple, an easy nature escape from the city.

name: Yoyogi Park
description: A large park next to Meiji Shrine, popular for picnics, street performers, and weekend gatherings of local subcultures.

name: Ameya-Yokocho Market
description: A bustling open-air market street near Ueno Station, born from a postwar black market, now selling food, spices, and clothing.

name: teamLab Planets
description: An immersive digital art museum where visitors walk barefoot through water and light installations, a uniquely Tokyo experience.

name: Nezu Shrine
description: One of Tokyo's oldest shrines, famous for its tunnel of vermilion torii gates and azalea garden in bloom season.
